title: Cross-survey latent consistency: the trunk feature of a place must be the same in all three photographs, not three fingerprints that happen to share a label
hypothesis: Experiment 2 produced exactly the clean negative its own pre-registration named: the three training photographs now converge (train_capture_diagnostics 0.060 / 0.053 / 0.088, 94-96% usable on each) while the held-out 2024 photograph barely moved (1.651 -> 1.583, 7% usable, 65% false fix). So 3 MB of weights and a 160-d pooled feature hold THREE separate pixel-fingerprints per 128 m cell with room to spare, and nothing in the current training signal objects: the soft cross-entropy only asks that three different feature vectors all point into the same logit direction, which a linear head satisfies trivially by carving three regions of feature space per cell. A fourth exposure of the same ground lands in none of those three regions, and the fix is confidently wrong. The missing signal is one that acts on the FEATURE the classifier reads, not on the classifier's answer: at every lattice position the paired batch already holds the same ground in all three surveys under one shared heading, so pull each survey's L2-normalised trunk feature toward the stop-gradient mean of the other surveys' features at that position (cosine loss). The classifier then cannot store three fingerprints, because the three must be one vector; whatever survives the pull is the structure the three photographs share (block layout, road geometry, building footprints, water) and the canopy/shadow/colour-balance cues that differ between a summer, a leaf-off and an early-spring survey are penalised. That is the library's L2 entry #1 (cross-survey latent consistency, the top rung of the SSL4EO ladder and the mechanism every cross-date aerial result was trained with), applied directly to the 160-d GAP feature rather than through a projector: a projector would let the feature keep its survey-specific content and discard it only in the projection, which is the opposite of what the linear cell head needs. No VICReg variance hinge: collapse is impossible while a 2,970-way cross-entropy is trained on the same vector. Output-level consistency (KL between the three cell distributions) would NOT work here, because experiment 2 already achieves near-identical argmaxes across the three surveys; the three-fingerprint solution satisfies output consistency perfectly and only feature-level consistency forbids it.
method: ONE change: add a cross-survey feature-consistency loss during training, with position-grouped mini-batches so every batch holds P positions x 3 captures. In model/model.py, training_outputs() additionally returns the pooled 160-d trunk feature f, and a new consistency_loss(f, n_caps) computes, for rows ordered position-major, fn = normalize(f).view(P, K, D), target_k = detach((sum_j fn_j - fn_k) / (K-1)), loss = mean_k(1 - <fn_k, target_k>). In model/train.py, mini-batches are drawn as whole positions (BATCH_SIZE // n_caps = 21 positions x 3 captures = 63 views) instead of shuffled single views, and the total loss becomes loss_fn(...) + CONS_WEIGHT * consistency_loss(...) with CONS_WEIGHT = 2.0. The per-epoch log line and train_info.json gain the mean cross-survey cosine and the consistency loss so the next experiment can read whether the term bit. Inference graph, ONNX export, decode, cell/offset targets, schedule and epoch budget are untouched.
expected_outcome: Diagnostic that must move for the mechanism to count as applied: the logged mean cross-survey cosine of the trunk feature rises above 0.9 by the last epoch (experiment 2 never measured it; three independent fingerprints would sit well below). Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.583 -> predicted 1.1-1.4, with false-fix rate falling from 65% to below 50% as features stop keying on one raster's intensities and texture, and usable rising from 7% to 15-30%. Training diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023) are expected to WORSEN mildly, from 0.05-0.09 to 0.1-0.3, because the model is forbidden its easiest solution; that is acceptable and is the sign the capacity moved from fingerprints to shared structure. Decision rules on the result: (a) cosine > 0.9 and 2024 improves -> supported; the next step layers L2 #2 (photometric + jitter augmentation) on top. (b) cosine > 0.9 but 2024 stays >= 1.5 -> invariance across these three surveys does not reach a fourth; the gap is then beyond what paired consistency alone can close and the next move is the distillation route (L2 #3) or augmentation. (c) cosine stays < 0.8 at CONS_WEIGHT 2.0 -> the cross-entropy out-muscled the term; rerun with a larger weight or a feature bottleneck before concluding anything about invariance. Standing check: the score must improve through usable_fix_rate, not through coverage collapsing (coverage must stay >= 0.2 and ideally near experiment 2's 72%).
eli5: Last time we showed the model three different photographs of Berlin at once, hoping it would learn what the city looks like. Instead it did the lazy thing: it memorised three separate photo albums and just agreed on the captions. Shown a fourth photograph, it had no album for it and guessed wrong, confidently. This experiment adds a rule during study: when you look at the same street corner in the summer photo, the winter photo and the spring photo, the picture you form in your head has to be THE SAME picture. That forces it to notice the things that do not change between photographs, like the shape of the blocks and the roads, and to stop leaning on the colour of the trees or the shadows that day. A fourth photograph should then look familiar.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small strided conv stack that turns the frame into a compact texture fingerprint (last layer 160 channels)

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: scores all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin and picks the tile this view belongs to — localization as multiple choice, not coordinate guessing

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the belief mass on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — a vote split across adjacent tiles still counts as knowing where you are; belief scattered across distant tiles still reads as unsure and the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: on top of the tile labels, the fingerprint the extractor produces for one place must be the SAME in all three survey photographs — each photo's fingerprint is pulled toward the average of the other two (cosine, no gradient through the target). Batches are built as whole places × three photos so the pull is always available. Labels, loss on tiles, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

implementation_brief:
Two files change: model/model.py and model/train.py. Copy nothing from older runs; the current code (which is runs/20261030_101727_experiment2/model_src/) is the starting point and most of it stays verbatim.

=== model/model.py ===
1. In CellLocNet, add a method `embed(self, x)` returning `self.features(x).mean(dim=(2, 3))` (the 160-d pooled feature). Change `training_outputs(self, x)` to compute `f = self.embed(x)` and return the THREE-tuple `(self.cls_head(f), torch.tanh(self.off_head(f)) * 0.5, f)`. Update `forward()` to unpack `logits, offset, _ = self.training_outputs(x)`; everything else in forward() (softmax, argmax, 3x3 mask, pooled centroid, offset nudge, clamp, stack) stays byte-identical, so the exported graph is unchanged.
2. Add a module-level function:
```
def consistency_loss(f: torch.Tensor, n_caps: int):
    """Cross-survey feature consistency. f is [P*K, D], rows ordered
    POSITION-MAJOR: row p*K + k is position p, capture k.
    Each capture's L2-normalised feature is pulled toward the detached
    mean of the OTHER captures' normalised features at the same position
    (cosine loss). Returns (loss, mean_cosine_detached). K == 1 -> (0, 1)."""
    if n_caps < 2:
        z = f.new_zeros(())
        return z, z + 1.0
    fn = F.normalize(f, dim=1).view(-1, n_caps, f.shape[1])      # [P, K, D]
    other = (fn.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True) - fn) / (n_caps - 1)   # [P, K, D]
    other = F.normalize(other.detach(), dim=2)
    cos = (fn * other).sum(dim=2)                                # [P, K]
    return (1.0 - cos).mean(), cos.detach().mean()
```
Keep `loss_fn` exactly as it is (same signature, same body). Keep CELL_PX, grid_dims, build_model, export_onnx, estimate_position untouched. Update the module docstring with one paragraph describing the consistency term (train-only, not in the graph).

=== model/train.py ===
3. Add a constant next to BATCH_SIZE: `CONS_WEIGHT = 2.0  # weight of the cross-survey feature-consistency loss`. Import `consistency_loss` from model.model.
4. `extract_chunk` already emits rows position-major (outer loop over positions, inner loop over captures) — keep it exactly as is, and add a comment stating that row p*K + k is position p, capture k, and that the consistency loss relies on this ordering.
5. In `train_area`, replace the mini-batch loop. Currently: `perm = torch.randperm(n)` over single views and `idx = perm[i:i + BATCH_SIZE]`. New: `n_pos = n // n_caps` (assert `n == n_pos * n_caps`), `pos_per_batch = max(1, BATCH_SIZE // n_caps)`, `pos_perm = torch.randperm(n_pos)`, and for `i in range(0, n_pos, pos_per_batch)`: `pidx = pos_perm[i:i + pos_per_batch]`; `idx = (pidx.unsqueeze(1) * n_caps + torch.arange(n_caps)).reshape(-1)`. This gives position-major batches of up to 21 positions x 3 captures = 63 views. Everything indexed by `idx` (x_u8, cell_idx, pos, cap_idx) stays as before.
6. In the step: `logits, off_pred, feat = model.training_outputs(xb)`; soft targets and residual offset target unchanged; `cons, cos_mean = consistency_loss(feat, n_caps)`; `loss = loss_fn(logits, off_pred, soft_t, off_t) + CONS_WEIGHT * cons`. Accumulate `cons_sum += cons.item() * len(idx)` and `cos_sum += float(cos_mean) * len(idx)` alongside loss_sum, and print `cons={cons_sum/seen:.4f} xsurvey_cos={cos_sum/seen:.4f}` on the per-epoch log line. Keep every existing log field (loss, top1, mean_max_softmax, views, lr, top1_by_capture).
7. In the returned info dict, keep every existing key and add: `"consistency_weight": CONS_WEIGHT`, `"final_consistency_loss": round(cons_sum/seen, 4)`, `"final_xsurvey_cosine": round(cos_sum/seen, 4)`, `"positions_per_batch": pos_per_batch`, and change `"capture_sampling"` to `"paired-position interleave, shared heading per position, position-grouped batches + cross-survey feature consistency"`. Update the module docstring with a short CROSS-SURVEY CONSISTENCY paragraph (what the term is, that batches are position-grouped, CONS_WEIGHT).

=== Contracts to preserve (the frozen scorer depends on them) ===
- CLI of model/train.py unchanged: `python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <dir> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`; it writes/appends `<out>/train_info.json` and prints the info dict as JSON on the last line.
- ONNX contract from model/model.py's docstring: one file at `<out>/models/<area>.onnx`, input `frame` 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output `uvc` = [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords in [0,1] and conf in [0,1]; the whole decode stays inside the graph; opset 17, dynamo=False. forward() must not reference the consistency machinery.
- Training reads only `buckets(meta, "train")` via load_scene; never open the eval capture (truedop_2024) in any form.
- Deployment gates: exported size must stay <= 4 MiB (unchanged architecture, 3.08 MB) and host latency proxy <= 250 ms (unchanged graph).
- Epoch budget: views per epoch unchanged (len(crops) * len(imgs)); the added cost is a few ops on a [63,160] tensor per step, so wall-clock stays ~58 min at 8 epochs on the M1.
- Genericity: n_caps == 1 (an area with a single capture) must still train: consistency_loss returns zero and the batch loop degenerates to plain batches of BATCH_SIZE views.

Sanity check before exiting: run `.venv/bin/python -c "import torch; from model.model import CellLocNet, consistency_loss; m = CellLocNet({'width': 7000, 'height': 6900}); x = torch.rand(6, 3, 128, 128); l, o, f = m.training_outputs(x); c, cs = consistency_loss(f, 3); print(l.shape, o.shape, f.shape, float(c), float(cs)); print(m(x).shape)"` and confirm shapes [6, n_cells], [6, 2], [6, 160], a finite loss, and forward output [6, 3]. Also build a tiny chunk (e.g. 4 positions x 3 captures) with the new batch indexing and assert every batch's rows come in consecutive triples of one position.
